comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE — the AWS code-review bot host, via an unpopulated OPTIONAL SSM parameter.
GitHub Actions is RULED OUT.

CHAIN OF EVIDENCE
1. env b2b5c498's event files are committed to the tickets branch by git committer
   'Rebar Bot <joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com>' — note the display name has a SPACE. This
   developer machine commits as 'RebarBotNava' (no space), same email, so the committer name
   is the discriminator between the two.
2. 'Rebar Bot' is the DEFAULT identity set by infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:35
   NAME="${REVIEWBOT_GIT_USER_NAME:-Rebar Bot}" — the AWS review-bot's store-write path.
3. REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY is referenced in infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh and the three
   GitHub Actions workflows — but NOT in reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh. The review-bot path
   sets a git identity and never arranges signing.
4. fetch-secrets.sh (~line 93) fetches the key OPTIONALLY and documents this exact outcome:
     'OPTIONAL: the Rebar Bot ed25519 authorship signing key (story 245e) ...
      Blank => the reviewbot writes unsigned (its types are gate-exempt, so this is
      attribution only).'
   The key is only materialized when the SSM slot rebar-bot-signing-key is non-empty. It is
   evidently empty on the running host, so the reviewbot writes unsigned exactly as designed.
5. Event-type profile corroborates: CREATE 1185 / LINK 1100 / REVIEW_RESULT 1187 are near
   equal — the per-review 'create a ticket, link it, record the result' shape of
   reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh — plus the enrichment-queue drain it also runs.
6. GitHub Actions EXONERATED: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml has an explicit
   'Materialize the Rebar Bot signing key' step, and its envs are 100% signed
   (rebar-bridge[bot] envs) / 50% (reconciler). Only b2b5c498 is 0%.

WHERE THE DESIGN NOTE UNDERSTATES THE IMPACT
The comment justifies unsigned writes as 'attribution only' because the reviewbot's types are
gate-exempt. But this env also writes 1185 CREATE events, and the envelope author resolves to
'Unknown' (author_id null, author_email empty, creation_channel null) — so it is not merely
unsigned, it is UNATTRIBUTED. 1185 tickets have no author of record.

OPERATOR ACTION
Populate the SSM parameter <prefix>/rebar-bot-signing-key with the Rebar Bot ed25519 key and
restart the review-bot container so fetch-secrets.sh materializes it and exports
REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY. Then confirm new events from that env carry author_sig and a
resolved author.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CORRECTION + CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE — the SSM key IS present. The host booted before it existed.

My previous comment concluded the SSM slot was unpopulated. That was WRONG. Checked with the
AWS CLI (metadata + length only, value never printed):
  /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key — EXISTS, SecureString, 433 chars, OpenSSH private key,
  LastModified 2026-07-14T09:47:09-07:00 (= 2026-07-14T16:47:09Z).

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — a boot-ordering gap:
  rebar-gerrit  i-00880b2c7f13527c5  LaunchTime 2026-07-13T16:19:58Z   (only running instance;
  per infra/terraform/ssm.tf it hosts the review-bot + auto-lander containers)
  SSM key populated                  2026-07-14T16:47:09Z

The instance booted ~24.5 HOURS BEFORE the key was added, and has not rebooted in the 27 days
since. fetch-secrets.sh runs at BOOT: it read the then-empty optional parameter, took the
'blank' branch (materialized no file), and wrote REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY= (empty) into the
container .env. Every event written since has therefore been unsigned.

This explains what an empty-slot theory could not: zero signed events EVER from this env
(0/8880) including 6062 in August, while the key is demonstrably present in SSM.

The code is not defective here — fetch-secrets.sh does materialize the key and does export
REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY into the .env (line 124) when the parameter is non-empty. The
defect is that a secret added AFTER boot is never picked up, and nothing surfaces the
resulting unsigned/unattributed writes.

OPERATOR ACTION (revised):
  Restart the review-bot/auto-lander containers (or reboot i-00880b2c7f13527c5) so
  fetch-secrets.sh re-runs and materializes the existing key. No new secret is needed.
  Then confirm new events from env b2b5c498 carry author_sig and a resolved author.

STILL WORTH FIXING IN CODE (the AC set stands):
  - a secret that appears after boot is invisible until a restart — worth a periodic refresh
    or a startup assertion;
  - an identity-less writer is silent — fsck should flag an env whose signed-rate is 0%;
  - the 1185 CREATEs from this env remain unattributed (author 'Unknown'), which the
    'attribution only' note in fetch-secrets.sh understates.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE — the key is never mounted INTO the container. My two earlier
diagnoses were both wrong; correcting the record.

WRONG #1: 'the SSM slot is unpopulated'. It is populated — /rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key,
SecureString, 433 chars, OpenSSH private key, LastModified 2026-07-14T16:47Z.

WRONG #2: 'the host booted before the key existed, so restart it'. Disproved on the host:
fetch-secrets.sh has re-run (the .env and the key file are both stamped 2026-08-09 15:58) and
compose-review-bot-1 restarted ~15:43 today — yet events at 16:16 are still unsigned. A
restart does not and cannot fix this.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (verified over SSM on i-00880b2c7f13527c5):
  inside the container:  REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=/opt/rebar/infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key
  that path inside:      ls: cannot access ... No such file or directory
  same path on the host: -rw------- 1 root root 432 Aug  9 15:58
  review-bot mounts:     gerrit_reviewbot -> /var/gerrit/site/reviewbot
                         gerrit_reviewbot_tickets -> /var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets
                         (no compose-dir bind mount, no key mount)

fetch-secrets.sh materializes the key to a HOST path and exports that HOST path into the
container through `env_file: - .env`. docker-compose.yml never bind-mounts the file, so the
variable points at a path that does not exist in the container's namespace. rebar reads the
var, cannot open the file, and silently falls back to unsigned. The env var being set is what
makes this invisible — every check short of opening the file passes.

FIX (code, not ops — no AWS-only action can resolve it):
  1. Bind-mount the key read-only into the review-bot service and set the CONTAINER-side path
     explicitly in the service `environment:` (overriding the host path inherited from
     env_file), e.g. ./rebar-bot-signing-key:/run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key:ro
  2. EDGE CASE: docker creates a DIRECTORY when bind-mounting a missing file. fetch-secrets.sh
     currently creates the file only when the SSM value is non-empty, so an unpopulated slot
     would break container start. Have fetch-secrets.sh always create the file (0600, possibly
     empty) so the mount is stable, and let an empty key mean unsigned.
  3. Make the failure LOUD: signing that is configured but unreadable should warn or fail,
     not silently downgrade — that silence is why this ran for a month.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AMENDMENT — my previous 'DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE' comment was still incomplete. There are TWO
compounding defects, and the mount is the SECOND-order one. Fixing only the mount would have
changed nothing.

DEFECT 1 (primary) — the identity never resolves, so signing is skipped before the key is
ever consulted.
  reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh sets the git identity REPO-LOCALLY on the tickets clone
  ($REVIEWBOT_TICKETS_DIR). But rebar resolves event attribution in
  _seam.attribution_fields(), which reads git config from config.repo_root() — inside the
  container that is /app (the rebar source clone), NOT the tickets store. Verified on the box:
    tickets clone identity : Rebar Bot / joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com   (set correctly)
    container GLOBAL identity: <empty>
  With no identity at repo_root, author_email() returns '' and resolve_current_identity()
  returns None — matching the observed envelopes exactly (author 'Unknown', author_email '',
  author_id null).
  _seam.py then gates signing on:   if author_id and signing_key:
  so a null author_id SHORT-CIRCUITS signing entirely. The key is never opened. This is why
  the events are not merely unsigned but UNATTRIBUTED, and why no 'could not sign' warning was
  ever logged — that warning lives inside the branch that never ran.

DEFECT 2 (secondary) — the key is not mounted into the container (as previously reported).
  Confirmed inside the container: REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY is set to the HOST path
  /opt/rebar/infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key, and ls of it returns No such file. The
  review-bot has only the two gerrit_reviewbot* mounts.

FIX PUSHED — Gerrit change 1567 (LLM-Review +1; Verified pending):
  - reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh also sets the identity with --global, so attribution resolves
    regardless of which repo_root rebar reads. --global is right here specifically because the
    container is dedicated to the review bot.
  - docker-compose.yml bind-mounts the key read-only at /run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key and
    sets the CONTAINER-side REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY in the service environment, overriding
    the host path inherited from env_file.
  - fetch-secrets.sh always creates the key file (empty when the SSM slot is blank), because
    docker turns a missing bind-mount source into a DIRECTORY and would break container start;
    the blank case now logs that the bot will write unsigned rather than passing silently.
  - Held-out unit test on the global identity, verified RED then GREEN.

DEPLOY: automatic. autodeploy.sh (rebar-autodeploy.timer, ~2 min) polls the GitHub mirror of
main and rebuilds the review-bot when its source changes; docker-compose.yml and
reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh are both in its BOT_PATHS. Note fetch-secrets.sh is NOT in
BOT_PATHS and only runs at boot, so its change will not execute on this deploy — harmless
here, because the key file already exists on the host (432 bytes, 2026-08-09 15:58), so the
new mount has a valid source.

STILL OPEN: the 8880 existing events cannot be retroactively signed or attributed. Disposition
to be decided (likely: document as an accepted pre-fix cohort and scope them out of
verify-authorship).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DISPOSITION (operator decision): the 8880 pre-fix events are ACCEPTED AS-IS. They will not be
retroactively signed or attributed — signatures cannot be created after the fact, and the
operator has confirmed the bar is signed-going-forward only.

Scope of this ticket is therefore: new events from the review-bot environment carry a resolved
author AND an author_sig. No backfill, no migration. If verify-authorship enforcement is ever
turned on (identity.require_authenticated is currently False), these events will need
grandfathering via identity.enforce_since rather than repair — that config key already exists
for exactly this purpose.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
THIRD DEFECT — ssh-keygen is not in the review-bot image. This was the actual blocker.

After change 89128b2e09 deployed (identity + key mount), I exercised the REAL signing seam
in-process inside the container rather than trusting the config state. Everything looked
right and it STILL did not sign:

  cfg signing_key : /run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key
  env var         : /run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key
  key readable    : True
  author          : Rebar Bot
  author_email    : joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com
  author_id       : 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d
  author_sig      : ABSENT
  SIGN RAISED     : SshKeygenUnavailable — ssh-keygen (OpenSSH) not found;
                    SSHSIG requires OpenSSH >= 8.9

rebar signs authorship with SSHSIG via `ssh-keygen -Y sign` (rebar.attest.sshsig). The
review-bot image is FROM python:3.12-slim installing only `git curl ca-certificates`, so
ssh-keygen was never present. sign_event_authorship raises, _seam catches it, event written
unsigned.

WHY IT STAYED HIDDEN FOR A MONTH: the exception is only logged as a WARNING, and it was never
even reached while author_id was null — _seam gates on `if author_id and signing_key`, so
defect 1 short-circuited before the try block. Fixing the identity is what let this surface.
That is also why config-level verification was insufficient: every observable input was
correct and the output was still unsigned.

FIX PUSHED — Gerrit change 1570: add openssh-client to Dockerfile.reviewbot (Debian bookworm
ships OpenSSH 9.2, clearing the 8.9 floor) + a static guard test asserting the image installs
it, verified RED then GREEN. Dockerfile.reviewbot is in autodeploy's BOT_PATHS, so submitting
rebuilds the image on the box.

FULL CAUSAL CHAIN (all three had to be fixed; any one alone leaves events unsigned):
  1. no global git identity  -> author_id null -> signing skipped silently   [89128b2e09]
  2. key not mounted         -> host path unreadable in container            [89128b2e09]
  3. ssh-keygen absent       -> SSHSIG raises -> caught -> unsigned          [1570]

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
VERIFIED ON THE LIVE BOX — signing now works.

After change 1570 merged and autodeploy rebuilt the review-bot image:
  ssh-keygen: /usr/bin/ssh-keygen   (was: MISSING)

Re-ran the IDENTICAL in-process probe that previously failed, inside the running container:
  author      : Rebar Bot
  author_email: joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com
  author_id   : 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d
  author_sig  : PRESENT          <- was ABSENT / SshKeygenUnavailable
  VERDICT: SIGNING WORKS

All three defects are closed:
  1. no global git identity  -> author_id null -> signing skipped silently   [89128b2e09]
  2. key not mounted         -> host path unreadable in container            [89128b2e09]
  3. ssh-keygen absent       -> SSHSIG raises -> caught -> unsigned          [1570]

CAVEAT ON THE EVIDENCE: the probe drives the real signing seam (_seam._apply_authorship) with
the real config, real key and real identity in the real container, and produces a real DSSE
signature — but it is in-process and writes nothing to the store. A genuine end-to-end event
has not been observed yet because the bot only writes when a review runs and there has been no
organic review activity since the deploy. A watcher is confirming the first real post-deploy
event from env b2b5c498 carries author_sig.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
END-TO-END CONFIRMED — real events, not the probe.

39 events written by env b2b5c498 since the change-1570 deploy, sampled across every type it
produces:
  CREATE         Rebar Bot  author_sig=True
  REVIEW_RESULT  Rebar Bot  author_sig=True
  LINK           Rebar Bot  author_sig=True
  CLAIM_ENRICH   Rebar Bot  author_sig=True
  TICKET_DIGEST  Rebar Bot  author_sig=True
  DONE_ENRICH    Rebar Bot  author_sig=True

Before: author 'Unknown', author_id null, author_sig absent, 0/8880 signed.
After:  author 'Rebar Bot', identity 594c-9dcf-5ad6-4e6d, signed.

The in-process caveat from the previous comment is now discharged: these are organic events
written by the bot's own review + enrichment activity and pushed to origin/tickets. Signing
works going forward, which was the agreed bar.

# Where the unsigned events come from

The project intends to sign every event, but ~11.2k ACTIVE events carry no `author_sig`.
Broken down by `env_id`, the cause is NOT diffuse — it is one environment.

## Evidence — signed rate per environment (active, non-SNAPSHOT events)

| env_id | signed | unsigned | signed% | last seen | top author |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b2b5c498 | 0 | 8880 | 0.0% | 2026-08-09T16:16 | Unknown (8880) |
| ade0f2ef (this host) | 9617 | 2186 | 81.5% | 2026-08-09T18:22 | RebarBotNava |
| reconciler | 95 | 93 | 50.5% | 2026-08-07 | reconciler |
| 4d084713 | 243 | 0 | 100% | 2026-08-08 | RebarBotNava |
| rebar-bridge[bot] envs | 10 | 0 | 100% | — | rebar-bridge[bot] |

**env b2b5c498 is the problem**: 8880 events, ZERO signed, every one authored "Unknown",
and still writing. Its envelopes carry `author: "Unknown"`, `author_id: null`,
`author_email: ""`, `author_sig: null`, `creation_channel: null` — i.e. NO identity is
configured in that environment at all, so both the authorship stamp and the signature are
skipped, and the creation-channel provenance feature is also a no-op there.

It is GROWING: 2818 events in 2026-07, 6062 in 2026-08.

Event types it writes: CLAIM_ENRICH 1500, TICKET_DIGEST 1496, DONE_ENRICH 1496,
REVIEW_RESULT 1187, CREATE 1185, LINK 1100, ENQUEUE_ENRICH 912, COMMENT 4. First seen
2026-07-10 20:58, right after the event-sourced enrichment queue landed (75d1a4672d,
2026-07-09) — so it looks like a headless drainer/automation environment. Note it also
CREATEs tickets and writes REVIEW_RESULTs unsigned, so the gap is not limited to the
enrichment queue.

## This host is NOT the problem
ade0f2ef's 2186 unsigned events are legacy: 772 from 2026-06, 1412 from 2026-07, and only
**2** in 2026-08. Signing works here now. Store-wide the June rate was 0% signed (the feature
did not exist), July 51%, August 48% — and the August figure is dragged down almost entirely
by b2b5c498.

## Not to be confused with the b636 restore
The b636 remediation restored 5041 unsigned historical events, which moved fsck's raw tally.
That was benign (they predate signing). THIS ticket is the separate, ongoing gap.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Identify the host/process behind env_id b2b5c498 (its events are the only lead:
      enrichment-queue drainer + CREATE/LINK/REVIEW_RESULT, first seen 2026-07-10).
- [x] That environment writes events with a resolved author identity AND an `author_sig`.
- [x] ~~`creation_channel` is stamped there too~~ — NOT DELIVERED, split to bug
      ed5c (hemophobic-vegetarian-mynah). Measured after this fix: 5 post-deploy
      CREATEs, creation_channel still None on all 5. Signing and channel-stamping
      are independent; fixing the identity did nothing for the channel.
- [x] ~~A guard makes an identity-less writer loud rather than silent~~ — NOT
      DELIVERED, split to bug ed5c. Still worth doing: the silence at three layers
      is exactly why this ran a month undetected.
      refuses, or fsck reports an env whose signed-rate is 0%, so this cannot recur unnoticed.
- [x] Disposition of the 8880 existing unsigned events: ACCEPTED AS-IS by operator
      decision. No backfill (signatures cannot be created retroactively). If
      enforcement is ever enabled, grandfather via identity.enforce_since.
      impossible — signatures cannot be forged retroactively; document them as an accepted
      pre-fix cohort scoped out of verify-authorship).
